retained_original_metadata.title: Local Markov swapping of decreasing neighboring rate parameters in step-initial discrete-time q-Hahn TASEP in the nonnegative-weight regime
retained_original_metadata.author: Leonid Petrov
retained_original_metadata.source_title: Parameter Permutation Symmetry in Particle Systems and Random Polymers
retained_original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The proof evaluates the swap action on all mixed q-moments and converts its beta-binomial sum into difference operators using the two-body boundary conditions. Acting with those operators inside the nested contour integrals removes exactly one rate and inserts its neighbor, identifying the whole joint law by bounded-moment uniqueness. It then removes the extra contour-separation condition by a finite rational continuation argument and a separate first-particle power-series argument.

proof_review.note: Complete author Theorem3.8 proof, including the n=1 continuation branch, is supplied. Select0<q<1, nu_i in(0,1) uniformly bounded away from1, and1<=gamma<1/sup_i nu_i so each jump distribution phi(q,gamma nu_i,nu_i) lies in the explicitly defined nonnegative range. Start from x_i(0)=-i and fix discrete t>=0; require nu_(n+1)<nu_n. The exact local swap3.7 acts only on x_n and produces the full joint fixed-time configuration law with those two parameters swapped. Existing multiparameter moment formula3.4 and quantum-binomial free/true evolution relation3.3 are prior background; the local contour boundary verification3.7 and full swap computation3.8 are written. The contour min/max condition3.5 is not retained as an extra conclusion hypothesis because the author explicitly removes it. Backward continuous-time processes, equilibrium convergence and beta-polymer variants are not separately counted.

retained_original_metadata.statement_scope: Theorem3.8 in the explicitly nonnegative parameter subregime0<q<1,0<nu_i<1,sup_i nu_i<1 and1<=gamma<1/sup_i nu_i, with step initial condition, integer fixed time and nu_(n+1)<nu_n. Exact swap3.7 and full joint law conclusion retained.

The selected stronger pointwise nonnegative-weight regime gamma<1/sup_i nu_i guarantees gamma nu_i<1, matching Definition3.1 for every particle. Preserve the original printed range in context and keep the selected subregime explicit; no original formula is replaced.
